html:
SMTO-EXE-0027 — Another job is still using what this task needs

GUID: a4b067bf-05ae-48d9-b559-3b445a79abbd
Slug: resource-reconciliation-not-eligible-live-owner
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • Your task is waiting because another job is still running, or may still be running, on the same files or resources. Your next command has not started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the recovery card in your task, select Wait until the job state changes, if that button is available. SMTO then watches the other job and starts your saved command by itself once that job lets go.
  2. If you know the other job is stuck or no longer needed, select Resolve forcefully by terminating job and read the warning first. Ending the other job frees the files or resources your task is waiting for.
  3. If neither choice fits, select Stop to end this task. Stopping avoids two jobs changing the same thing at the same time.

What success looks like

  • The card shows the other job has ended, and your task continues with its next command.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start the same command elsewhere while the other job may still be running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Baseline acceptance was refused, or not offered, because a blocking job is not proven ended, released and inactive, another active job holds a conflicting resource claim, or the run cannot currently resume.

What this means

  • Baseline acceptance found a blocker that failed ended/released/no-active-execution requirements or another conflicting owner. The decision view also uses this category whenever baseline eligibility is not established. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Baseline acceptance found a blocker that failed ended/released/no-active-execution requirements or another conflicting owner. The decision view also uses this category whenever baseline eligibility is not established.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect blocker liveness, resource claims, active-execution certainty and any conflicting peer; do not assume the absence of visible output proves completion.

How to fix it

  • No corrective action is required for this informational outcome.
  • Inspect the blocking jobs listed in resource_reconciliation_request.details (liveness_state, resource_claim_state, active_execution_possible) and any peer job with a conflicting claim (GatewayJobs.accept_current_state_baseline). Let them end, or use the recovery reset action when eligible; baseline acceptance stays unavailable until every blocker is ended, released and inactive.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • All baseline prerequisites hold for current resources before the normal recovery flow accepts a decision.

What not to do

  • Do not turn this status into an automatic retry or a new execution request.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
